hooks.text: A cosmic Death Star was once feared to be pointed at Earth.
Eighty-four hundred light-years away, a pinwheel star system once threatened Earth.
Astronomers once panicked that a rotating stellar pinwheel targeted Earth.

title: The Death Star System Pointed at Earth
description: WR 104 is a pinwheel-shaped star system once feared to be pointed at Earth for a gamma-ray burst.

beats.text: A cosmic Death Star was once feared to be pointed at Earth.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a Wolf-Rayet star emitting a gamma-ray burst
queries: Wolf Rayet star supernova artist concept

beats.text: Deep in the constellation Sagittarius lies WR 104, located about eight thousand four hundred light-years from Earth.
At its heart, a massive Wolf-Rayet star and an OB companion orbit each other every eight months.
beats.visual: Illustration of colliding stellar winds in a binary star system

beats.text: Their powerful stellar winds slam together, creating a spinning pinwheel nebula over two hundred astronomical units wide.
beats.visual: Infrared telescope image showing the WR 104 pinwheel nebula

beats.text: Early imaging suggested Earth was looking directly down the rotational axis, sparking panic over a lethal gamma-ray burst.
beats.visual: Diagram of Earth ozone layer depletion by cosmic radiation

beats.text: Recent Keck Observatory research revealed that the actual stellar orbit is tilted thirty to forty degrees away from us.
beats.visual: Keck Observatory telescope facility on Maunakea
queries: W. M. Keck Observatory twin telescopes

beats.text: Earth is safely out of the firing line, proving why a cosmic Death Star was once feared to be pointed at Earth.
emphasis: safely out of the firing line
beats.visual: Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory, ESO
